svg.text: Testbed block diagram rev 2 — 120 W, 48 V → 12 V (after the 2026-10-08 circuit review; scope option B as built, option-C parts dashed)

blue = feeder node, orange = rack node, red = fault paths and breakers, grey = control, safety and the HIL plug-in. Power wiring in black. One star ground at the storage-bank negative; the lab supply (−) is bonded to it (feeder breaker is high-side, so the return is never opened).

Changed vs rev 1 (SCHEMATIC_DESIGN rev 2 change log): ① both breakers high-side, isolated drivers, fail-safe = pull-UP + inverting · ② freewheel diode D_fw across R_f48 + L_f48 · ③ TVS across Q_brk · ④ 74HC221 one-shot, arm key on CLR · ⑤ all gate drivers from a separate 12 V adapter · ⑥ F2 moved to the converter output

⑦ power-up order / precharge · ⑧ 100 V parts everywhere on the 48 V side · ⑨ anti-alias filter corrected to Butterworth, −3 dB 100.6 kHz, −48 dB at 400 kHz · ⑩ INA240A2 for ×50 · ⑪ fault resistor = target − measured coil DCR
⑫ two more converter buy criteria (start-up into 66 mF, no reverse boost) · ⑬ supply (−) bonded to the star, scope ground clips on the star only, diff probe on the feeder side
+ start-up into 66 mF, no reverse boost ⑫
D_fw Schottky 30 A across R + L ②
(D_fw also takes the coil current when Q_brk opens)
shunt → INA240A2 ×50 → AA 100 kHz ⑨ → ADC1
v_bus ÷21 → buffer → AA → ADC2 · 500 kSa/s DMA
TRIP → LED + HIL input (option C: + Q_fb driver)
ONSET / TRIP test pins · SYNC in · USB record · CAN-FD
JP1/JP2: replay inputs (DAC or HIL) in place of the sensors
shunt → INA240A1 ×20 → AA 100 kHz ⑨ → ADC1
v_out ÷5.3 → buffer → AA → ADC2 · 500 kSa/s DMA
TRIP (active high) → Q_brk iso driver + HIL input
ONSET / TRIP test pins · SYNC in · USB record · CAN-FD
JP1/JP2: replay inputs (DAC or HIL) in place of the sensors
CAN-FD: summary 16 B within 20 µs, features after (DEVIATIONS #13)
workload profile → 5 load gates (staircase ramps, two-tier cadence)
FAULT_B → 74HC221 one-shot 5 ms (arm key on CLR) ④ → Q_f48 driver
POL-UVLO on v_out (9.6 V / 100 µs → loads off) · SYNC out (BNC)
DAC1/DAC2 1 MSa/s replay → JP1/JP2 of a node (latency test, M4)
demo controller: fault command → HIL digital input (F8) · USB CLI (bench_run.py)
option C adds FAULT_A → one-shot A 10 ms → Q_f8 driver
separate 12 V adapter (not the bench bus)
→ 2 × iso DC-DC (12→15 V, 1 W) → UCC5350 / ADuM4120
breaker drivers: pull-UP + inverting ⇒ unpowered node = OPEN
4 analog outs → JP1/JP2 of both nodes (0–10 V, 3:1 pad)
2 TRIPs + fault command → HIL digital inputs
HIL digital out → SYNC · model breaker opens on TRIP
fallback: DAC replay + post-trip waveform switch
ch1 SYNC · ch2 rack shunt (diff probe ≥ 10 MHz, before the filter)
ch3 ONSET · ch4 TRIP → onset-to-trip latency, raw fault front
ground clips only on the star; feeder side by diff probe ⑬
PC via USB isolator on the node links
Power-up order ⑦ and safety rules

1 nodes + bench control on USB (TRIP = 0 → breakers close) → 2 driver adapter on → 3 K1 closed with the supply OUTPUT OFF → 4 supply output on (its ramp precharges C_bus / C_in: no 200 A inrush, C_in never sees 58 V) → 5 arm key only for a fault run.

Every node reset opens its breaker (fail-safe) — expected, not a fault. Fault runs: second person present, professor's sign-off, E-stop within reach, ≤ 130 A ≤ 5 ms by hardware. Stored energy 4.2 J (bank) + 0.15 J (bus): burn/spatter hazard at the fault switch only.

Not built: bolted 800 V-side faults (Layer 1; abusive to the supply). Not on the bench node: isolation, external SAR ADC — product items, said so on the slide. Option C adds Q_fb, the feeder fault injector and one-shot A (dashed above).

Sheets: 1 power (rev 2) · 2 node front end (rev 2: filter values, INA240A2, 1 kΩ + clamp input protection with R1 → 100 Ω) · 3 control and drivers (rev 2: HC221, isolated breaker drivers, adapter supply, pull-up).
Values are design values; every element is measured before the first fault run and the bench dataset is regenerated from the measured values (SCALING_SHEET §5.4).
What the bench proves: the same relay firmware, trained on simulated bench events from measured parameters, deciding on real sensors and real faults at 120 W (judges' doubt 3).
The HIL plug-in proves the full-scale 800 V design in closed loop (doubts 1–2, and the live "trigger a fault" demo). Both use the same node firmware; only settings and a jumper differ.
